Photo By - Reuters Connect. CJ Bailey (11) leads NC State against Davis Warren (8) and Stanford. In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . NC State vs Stanford: Quick Hits Why does Stanford need this? Three straight road games follow this, but that includes a trip up the road to Cal. Not to get all basic here, but the Cardinal have scored seven points or fewer in the four losses, and 34 or more in the three wins. The ground game has been non-existent against everyone but Elon and Hawaii. NC State is fantastic at keeping the chains moving. Stanford doesn't get to the quarterback and will struggle to hit Wolfpack star CJ Bailey enough to get off the field. Why Stanford Will Win Okay, context time. Yeah, Stanford's offense was putrid in the four losses. One of those came against a nasty Duke defense Durham, and the other three losses were to Miami, Notre Dame, and a Wake Forest team whose only loss is to the Hurricanes. This is one of those focus-test moments for the ACC team from the Eastern Time Zone. This will end around 2 am NC State time, and while these are college kids who can certainly stay awake, the rhythm will be thrown off. NC State vs Stanford Prediction, Betting Lines Don't just blow this off as a layup win for NC State before getting back on the plane to go deal with bigger and better things. The Wolfpack have had to deal with a whole ton of adversity this season, and they keep coming back, but it's 0-2 on the road, and Stanford is 3-1 at home, with that one loss coming to Miami. NC State doesn't have the pass rush to overwhelm the Cardinal backfield, but it'll be just okay enough to get out with a tough late-night win. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

Find out as we break down this fascinating Big Ten matchup at the Big House this Saturday. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Josh Hoover of Indiana and Tommy Carr of Michigan. My Indiana vs. Michigan prediction backs the Wolverines to keep it close during Saturday afternoon's Big Ten showdown. With Bryce Underwood taking a seat and Tommy Carr making his first collegiate start, Michigan's offense could get a refreshing change of pace. However, I still expect both defenses to dominate from start to finish. Find out why I'm backing the Wolverines in my latest college football picks ahead of Saturday's noon ET kickoff on FOX. TOP PICK Who will win Indiana vs Michigan: Michigan +7.5 If this is the end for Bryce Underwood and the start of the Tommy Carr era, Michigan is the play on Saturday. The freshman threw for just 47 yards while completing five of seven attempts after replacing Underwood during a win over Penn State. He also rushed for 36 yards and found pay dirt in the fourth quarter. Anything is better than forcing Underwood out there, especially when he's been a turnover machine. The Indiana Hoosiers are coming off a tough loss to the Ohio State Buckeyes, a game they were just inches away from winning. Some will see that heartbreak and run to bet the Hoosiers this week, but this Michigan team catching 7.5 points is too good to pass up. The Wolverines boast a defense allowing the fewest yards per play in the country , the second-fewest total yards, and just over 16 points per game. I snagged +7.5, but I endorse Michigan down to +7. Indiana vs Michigan Over/Under pick: Under 41.5 Look at that beautiful key number of 41 and the hook! For Michigan to cover in this matchup, the Under will need to be the play, even with Carr running the show. With this being the freshman's first collegiate start, he's likely to hit some speed bumps along the way. Head coach Kyle Whittingham will probably take a more conservative approach, leaning on designed runs while Carr continues to develop into the passer this team needs him to be going forward. Indiana has done an incredible job limiting scoring this season, with Big Ten opponents averaging just 18.5 points per game against the Hoosiers . I envision a 20-17 ballgame at its ceiling. I'd take this under down to 40, at most. Indiana vs Michigan combo This game script sets up nicely for a correlated parlay. Michigan lost tough games against Iowa and Minnesota, but a gut-check win over Penn State threw the season a lifeline. Penn State tapped out long ago, Oregon isn't anything special, and Iowa and UCLA, while great, still have to survive the second half of the Big Ten season. The winner in Ann Arbor on Saturday has a chance to do some big things. Indiana vs Michigan: Quick Hits Michigan has winnable dates against Rutgers on the road before hosting Michigan State. And then comes the problem – at Oregon, UCLA, at Ohio State. The Hoosiers get three of their last four games at home, getting Minnesota and USC next. Indiana beat Michigan 20-15 in 2024. Before that, the Wolverines won 26 of the previous 27 games going back to 1987, with the lone loss in the shortened 2020 season. How To Watch Indiana vs Michigan Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, MI – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why Indiana Will Win It's crazy how this works. Had Nick Marsh been able to get one foot just a few inches over to one side, Indiana would be the unquestioned No. 1 team in both polls, and it would be ridiculous to give anyone else a single first-place vote. In other words, losing to Ohio State matters, of course, but … not really. The Hoosiers are still fantastic. Michigan still can't score. There were the 52 points hung up on UTEP, and last week's 21-18 win over Penn State was the only other time the offense scored more than 19 points. It's been a struggle, and the running game won't get better against the fourth-best run defense in America. Why Michigan Will Win Could Tommy Carr really be the answer? Yes, he's legendary Lloyd Carr's grandson, and yes, he's the younger brother of Notre Dame's CJ Carr, but he's at Michigan. The guy is talented. It's too easy to suggest that Bryce Underwood was the reason Michigan's offense was so bad, but he wasn't getting the job done – to be nice about it. All Carr did was hit 5-of-7 passes for 47 yards along with a rushing score. There's a new vibe now on offense, and … Indiana vs Michigan Prediction, Betting Lines It gets said every week, and it's important to keep bringing it up. The Michigan defense is fantastic. It's fourth in the nation overall, fantastic against the run, and it'll give the Indiana offense a whole slew of problems. The Wolverine running game still won't work, but Carr will be okay and the defense will keep this close until late. Like the Northwestern, Nebraska, and Ohio State games, though, Indiana will have to come up big in the fourth quarter. Like it did against the Wildcats and Huskers, it will. Rotoworld Player News NFL Player News Fantasy Sports Rotoworld Home Betting Betting Home Profile Login Vaughn Dalzell , Vaughn Dalzell After suffering heartbreak in a 19-15 loss to #4 Ohio State last week, the #6 Indiana Hoosiers (6-1) are on the road with no time to sulk. This week the Hoosiers head to The Big House and take on a rested Michigan Wolverines (4-2) team. Michigan enters with a new sense of hope for the rest of the season. The Wolverines are fresh off a bye week and announced that Tommy Carr will be starting against Indiana, not the $12 million dollar man Bryce Underwood . Carr replaced Underwood in the second half against Penn State and led a comeback charge to win 21-18 after Michigan trailed 3-0 at the half. Carr had 83 total yards and a rushing touchdown in the second half of the win, which was encouraging for Michigan supporters. On the flip side, this will be Carr’s first collegiate start, and it’s against Curt Cignetti and Indiana coming off a loss (33-3 record with Cignetti). Yikes. Throw him to the wolves why don’t ya? Indiana is still favored to make the College Football Playoff despite the loss to Ohio State. The Hoosiers’ only ranked game remaining is against USC on Nov. 14, and the Trojans play Ohio State the week prior, so it’s a good spot for Indiana. Indiana likely finishes the regular season 11-1, and it’s a rematch between the Buckeyes and Hoosiers in the Big Ten Championship Game. The only question then would be: is Julian Sayin back? That’s a question and conversation for another day. The Hoosiers’ run game was stalled in the loss to Ohio State. Indiana ran for 73 yards on 29 carries (2.5 ypc) and recorded zero explosive runs. The offense relied heavily on Josh Hoover , Charlie Becker , and Nick Marsh to cook. Becker and Marsh caught 12 of Hoover’s 20 completions (60%) and 222 of the 296 passing yards (75%). Hoover had a season-high 40 pass attempts, his only game over 30, and Indiana shouldn’t have to pass as much this week, or again for the rest of the regular season. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Indiana vs Michigan Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Time: 12:00 PM Eastern Site: Michigan Stadium City: Ann Arbor, MI TV/Streaming: Fox Game Odds for Michigan vs Indiana The latest odds as of Thursday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Indiana Hoosiers (-278), Michigan Wolverines (+225) Spread: Indiana -7 (-112) Total: 41.5 points Michigan Wolverines Head Coach: Kyle Whittingham 2026 Record: 4-2 (1-2) Offensive Points Per Game: 22.7 (106th) Defensive Points Per Game: 16.1 (T-20th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 61st 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 8th The Michigan Wolverines Offense: After six games, Kyle Whittingham has pulled the plug and benched Bryce Underwood . Tommy Carr , brother of Notre Dame’s CJ Carr, will get the start. What to expect from Carr and the Wolverines’ offense is up in the air. Carr had seven drives to work with in the second half versus Penn State and finished with 47 passing yards, 36 rushing yards, and a rushing score. Michigan scored 21 second-half points after trailing 3-0 at halftime. Michigan’s Team Total for this game is 16.5, and Carr is projected at Over or Under 137.5 passing yards and 15.5 rushing yards. That doesn’t sound very promising coming off the bye week. Michigan did run for 211 yards and three touchdowns against Penn State, but the Hoosiers’ rush defense ranks first in rush defense per PFF. Michigan Player to Watch on Offense: QB Tommy Carr Carr led the second-half comeback charge against Penn State and scored on three out of seven drives despite not totaling 100 yards in the half. After paying Bryce Underwood $12 million, Carr comes in with much lower expectations and should thrive over the next few games, but this is a rough spot. The positive is that Michigan had a bye week to work with Carr and see what makes him comfortable, but making your first career start against Curt Cignetti, as Indiana is coming off only the third loss in Cignetti’s Hoosiers coaching career, does not sound ideal for Carr. The Michigan Wolverines Defense: The Michigan defense forced Penn State’s Rocco Becht into three turnovers (2 INT, 1 FUM) in the last game and held the rushing attack to 65 yards on 30 carries (2.2 ypc). Penn State scored twice in the fourth quarter to pull the score within one possession, but Michigan shut the door the following possessions and held Penn State to four punts in the first half. Michigan ranks second-best in the country in rush defense per PFF, behind only Indiana, and the Wolverines are top 25 in pressure (11th) and coverage grades (18th). The defense will have to carry them on Saturday to stay within striking distance. Michigan Player to Watch on Defense: DL John Henry Daley John Henry Daley entered the bye week on a four-game sack streak and has thrived at Michigan. Daley played for Whittingham at Utah the last two seasons (12.5 sacks) after starting his career at BYU. Daley’s stock has been rising this season after a career-high 11.5 sacks with the Utes. Daley has 4.0 sacks over five games in his pocket with 1.5 versus Oklahoma, 1.0 versus UTEP and Penn State, plus a 0.5 sack against Iowa. Indiana has the second-best-rated pass-blocking grades, but Hoover has been sacked twice in three out of six games, but not against Ohio State last week. Hoover has 18 touchdown passes to no picks and tossed a season-high 40 passes for 296 yards versus OSU. Due to the trailing game script and inability to run the ball, Hoover was forced into obvious passing situations. The Hoosiers ran for 73 yards on 29 carries (2.5 ypc), with the longest run of the day being eight yards. Indiana should struggle running on Michigan’s front seven, but the game script shouldn’t be the same leaving Hoover, Turbo Richard , and Lee Bebee Jr. in better positions to succeed. Indiana Player to Watch on Offense: WR Nick Marsh If Nick Marsh had watched more Antonio Brown growing up, Indiana would have beaten Ohio State and been No. 1 in the AP Poll. The Hoosiers were so close to winning, but Marsh couldn’t toe tap a dime from Hoover. I am curious how Marsh responds this week and if they go to him early and often. Marsh only had three receptions versus Ohio State, but turned them into 57 yards and a touchdown. Charlie Becker had nine catches for 165 yards. A week ago at Nebraska, Marsh went for a career-high 187 yards and two touchdowns on six receptions. The Indiana Hoosiers Defense: Indiana’s defense picked Ohio State’s Julian Sayin off twice and gave him a potential season-ending injury in a bruising battle between two top-five teams. The Hoosiers held the Buckeyes to 78 rushing yards on 28 carries (2.1 ypc) and sacked Ohio State a season-high four times. Indiana will have a much softer matchup against a Michigan offense that’s outside the top 100 in points per game. Indiana Player to Watch on Defense: DL Stephen Daley Stephen Daley had his three-game sack streak snapped against Ohio State. Daley had 1.0 sack versus Northwestern and 2.0 sacks each against Ohio State and at Nebraska. Daley is another riser this season, and he’s one sack from surpassing his career-high of 5.5 sacks last year with Indiana. Daley has also forced two fumbles this year and is at 16.5 sacks and five forced fumbles over his five-year career. away.blurb: Moore, the Wolverines’ starting safety and one of four team captains, center Jake Guarnera, right guard Brady Norton and tackle Blake Frazier are all listed as questionable for Saturday’s game against No. 6 Indiana on Saturday (12 p.m., FOX). Michigan submitted its first player availability report of the week to the Big Ten on Wednesday, with seven players ruled out, another seven listed as questionable and one as probable. Moore had to be carted to the locker room during the Wolverines’ 21-18 win over Penn State last Saturday, an injury that appeared to occur when he laid out for his third-quarter interception. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham wouldn’t categorize Moore’s injury as particularly serious after the game, calling it “nothing that’s long term” and “he’ll be OK.” Norton missed last week’s game with an undisclosed injury, a blow to Michigan’s already-depleted offensive line. Guarnera, on the player report again this week, was listed as a game-time decision but played. Frazier, a starter at left tackle during Michigan’s first two games and right tackle for the last four, is new to the report this week. Elsewhere along the offensive line, starting right tackle Andrew Sprague will miss his fifth consecutive game with an undisclosed issue while sophomore Andrew Babalola, still waiting to make his collegiate debut, is probable. Another surprise: Michigan starting defensive tackle Enow Etta is questionable. The Wolverines’ defensive line has been a strength of the team this year, ranking 13th nationally in rushing defense (90 yards per game), and not having Etta would be a major blow up front. Starting defensive end Dom Nichols is questionable to play for a fourth straight game, though he’s appeared in the last three. away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Ten SEC teams fall into the 4-1 to 2-2 range after Auburn pulled off a stunning 27-24 win at Georgia last week. The rest of the AU Tiger schedule is challenging, but if you can beat Georgia in Sanford Stadium, the bar gets set a little higher. LSU lost both of its road games – Ole Miss and Kentucky – but it's been an unstoppable force at home, destroying Clemson by 41, Texas A&M by 29, and beating Mississippi State 31-0 last week. The Bayou Bengal Tigers are still among the most dangerous and talented teams in the country on the right day, but, like Auburn, one more loss and that's about it for the SEC and College Football Playoff dreams. LSU vs Auburn: Quick Hits LSU gets a nasty run over the next three games, but Alabama and Texas are home games before going to Tennessee. Auburn goes to Ole Miss next, and three of the last four SEC games are on the road. LSU beat Auburn 48-18 when the two last met in 2023 and has won six of the last eight games. The Auburn offense wants to move at a lightning-fast pace, and Lane Kiffin's attack is at its best when it's going 150 miles per hour. The one big difference is control of the tempo. LSU is amazing at dominating the time of possession battle, and it should hold the ball for large chunks of time. Auburn is 133rd in the nation, keeping the ball for fewer than 27 minutes per game. As much as the offense matters, though, it's the LSU defense that has to keep Auburn from getting out of third gear. LSU is second in the nation in sacks, and AU can't keep quarterback Byrum Brown from getting popped. Why Auburn Will Win It really is impressive. LSU looks and plays like it has 14 guys on the field who are all twice as fast as everyone else … at home. The LSU offense wasn't too bad in the losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky, but the defense occasionally played like it didn't attend the last three classes before the test. It's not a coincidence. LSU has allowed more than 145 passing yards just two times this season. Take a wild guess which teams got it going through the air. In case you were wondering, the 21-15 win over Vanderbilt is the only time Auburn failed to throw for at least 145 yards. LSU vs Auburn Prediction, Betting Lines Let's get it out of the way. It wasn't funny when the line was first written in 1999, and it's even more brutal now, but college football is nothing without its traditions, so … "This is our five-star, all-time, can't-miss lock of the century for this week … the Tigers are going to win." Really, how did Auburn beat Georgia? First of all, Auburn is just that good. But also, it actually held its own in the time of possession battle – the defense held up and wasn't gassed late. That, and it helped to get be +3 in turnover margin. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will throw his customary interception – although he didn't give one away for the first time all year in last week's win over Mississippi State – but LSU's control of the clock and the narrative on the lines will be enough to finally get a road win. picks.headline: Auburn vs LSU early predictions, picks, odds for Week 8
picks.blurb: Auburn is ready to return to its home field after pulling off one of college football's most stunning upsets in Week 7 over then-No. 1 Georgia. Auburn won the turnover battle, 3-0, and ran the football efficiently, outgaining the Bulldogs, 192-113, in what was arguably its cleanest game of the season. LSU bounced back from Week 6's loss at Kentucky by shutting out then-No. 19 Mississippi State in Baton Rouge, 31-0. The Tigers took advantage of a Kamario Taylor-less Mississippi State squad, outgaining them, 379-291. This week marks the second straight week Auburn has had to prepare for a top SEC squad in terms of production. LSU is the SEC-best in total offense (504 yards per game), defense (256.4 yards allowed per game), first downs (28 per game), and passing (308 yards per game). The Bayou Bengals rank in the top five in several other categories, including points per game, points allowed per game, and time of possession. However, Auburn proved in Athens last week that stats do not matter and that being more physical can be enough to win. A key storyline to follow is the battle between two first-year head coaches, Alex Golesh and Lane Kiffin. Kiffin is 2-3 against Auburn as a head coach, and has won his last two games against the Tigers (2022 and 2023 at Ole Miss). Golesh has never faced Kiffin as a head coach. Another storyline is the rivalry renewal between two old-school SEC West teams. Auburn and LSU have not played since the 2023 season, and LSU leads the series, 30-24-1 over Auburn . However, Auburn proved last week at Georgia that stats don't matter and the more physical team will likely win. picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. He may be reached at 865-342-6284 or john.adams@knoxnews.com. Published: Oct 22, 2026 · 10:00 AM EDT The Fearless Prediction had wavering confidence in Josh Heupel and the Tennessee Volunteers last week and could not have been more wrong. Tennessee's defense is absolutely legit, and the offense showed remarkable physical and mental toughness in a dominating 26-10 victory over Alabama . We won't doubt the Big Orange again. (Looks at schedule.) If you had to explain to a friend who knows nothing about college football what a “trap game” was, Tennessee's upcoming visit to South Carolina potentially fits the bill. The Vols do not play well at Williams-Brice. Tennessee's loss in 2016 put it on the road to losing the SEC East. The Vols' loss in 2022 probably cost them a spot in the 4-team College Football Playoff and saw their star QB Hendon Hooker rip up his knee, ending his college career. There's also the matter of Connor Stalions and how he may or may not have assisted South Carolina. College football rarely disappoints. In terms of this season, the Vols are coming off an impressive victory and a rivalry win, no less. Can they put that in the rearview? As for South Carolina, Shane Beamer is coaching for his job. Last time out, the Gamecocks pulled off a surprising win at Florida , and now are well rested following a bye week. Tennessee's defense is good. Really good. Following a 5-sack performance against Alabama, the Vols have 30 sacks on the season, tops in the FBS. They are also 6th in the country in tackles for loss with 58. Against the Crimson Tide, the Vols stopped 11 of 13 third-down attempts and allowed only 54 rushing yards. Defensive linemen Xavier Gilliam and Tyree Weathersby are the modern-day Undertaker and Kane, causing havoc with a combined 11.5 sacks and 18.5 tackles for loss. Linebackers Amare Campbell and Arion Carter are at the top of the tackle table with 46 and 43, respectively. The Vols have also collected 13 turnovers, tied for 10th-best in the FBS. New defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has been a revelation, leading one of the best groups in the country. As for that Tennessee offense, why don't they just build the whole plane out of DeSean Bishop? He's now averaging nearly 120 rushing yards per game with a healthy 6 yards per carry. Against Alabama, he had 159 rushing yards and 2 scores. Having Bishop takes a lot off the plate of redshirt freshman QB George MacIntyre, who seems to have cemented his place as Tennessee's starter. He'll get the call for his 2nd career road start on Saturday. As for South Carolina, the Gamecocks were left for dead a couple of weeks ago, as was their head coach, Shane Beamer. They had lost 3 straight, including a crushing OT loss to Kentucky . But then came a startling 38-19 victory over Florida. QB LaNorris Sellers has a combined 291.5 yards passing and rushing, with 14 combined TDs. South Carolina needs a big game from Sellers if it is going to win on Saturday. Tennessee doesn't give up many big plays, but needs to be aware of WR Nyck Harbor, averaging 16.4 yards per reception. RB Matt Fuller is gaining 81 yards per game on the ground. Defensively, senior LB Justin Okoronkwo leads the Gamecocks with 43 tackles. Lineman Tomiwa Durojaiye has 4.5 tackles for loss. If special teams are to be a factor, Tennessee's Cooper Ranvier has made 10 of 11 FGs, South Carolina's Malik Orsan has made 8 of 10 FGs. By Parker Gillam Published: Oct 21, 2026 · 7:58 PM EDT Tennessee is set to pay a visit to South Carolina this Saturday, and the Volunteers are still riding high following their upset win over Alabama last weekend. But Columbia has been far from kind to the Volunteers in recent memory, as they've dropped 6 of their last 8 contests at Williams-Brice Stadium heading into this one. That was one of the many points ESPN's Greg McElroy made in his breakdown of the game during an episode of his “Always College Football” show, and the former Alabama quarterback is actually picking the Gamecocks to pull off the upset. “I'm gonna take South Carolina to win this game, 27-24, and I think they're gonna do it on the ground,” McElroy said . “They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war, and looked amazing doing it. But we've seen teams elevate and then come back down to Earth the following week, and I think that's what's gonna happen here.” RELATED: Looking for the latest spreads and totals? McElroy elaborated by saying that LaNorris Sellers and Matt Fuller will be able to find plenty of success on the ground, with him adding that South Carolina ‘s downfield weapons will create enough explosive plays to counteract anything Tennessee throws at them. “Tennessee linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game,” McElroy said. “Because that would keep the Gamecocks out of third and long, which is where Tennessee's sacks live.” Parker is currently the sports editor for Gulf Coast Media in Foley, Alabama. picks.headline: Can Tennessee football maintain momentum at South Carolina? Our pick
picks.blurb: News Sports Business Go Knoxville Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Can Tennessee football maintain momentum at South Carolina? Our pick Emmett Siegel Knoxville News Sentinel Oct. 22, 2026, 5:07 a.m. ET The No. 11 Tennessee Volunteers will face the South Carolina Gamecocks on October 24. South Carolina is looking to build on a recent win against Florida after a slow start to their season. Key players for the Gamecocks include quarterback LaNorris Sellers and edge rusher Dylan Stewart. Tennessee's defense has been dominant this season, leading the SEC in several key statistical categories. Tennessee football is tasked with avoiding a letdown after a convincing win against Alabama, and it'll have to do so in a hostile road environment. The No. 11 Vols (6-1, 3-1 SEC) play South Carolina (3-3, 1-3) at Williams-Brice Stadium on Oct. 24 (3:30 p.m., ESPN). Tennessee's last trip to Columbia in 2022 ended with a blowout loss that knocked it out of College Football Playoff contention. It'll try to avoid a similar fate this year and maintain its footing in the CFP race before its open week. Here's what to know about the matchup. South Carolina's season started slow before Florida win Just a few weeks ago, it looked as though South Carolina's season was hanging on by a thread. The Gamecocks started 0-3 in SEC play. After a 4-8 season last year, coach Shane Beamer's seat was getting scorching hot. But they bought themselves a bit more time with a 38-19 win at Florida before the open week. And while the game before that was a home loss to Kentucky, South Carolina was one two-point conversion stop away from winning in overtime. Beamer still needs a decent finish to quiet discussions about his job security, but his team has shown it is capable of beating just about anyone in the SEC. In 2024, with many of the same key players, the Gamecocks went 9-4 and nearly made the CFP. LaNorris Sellers, Dylan Stewart star at premium positions South Carolina has game changers at premium positions on both offense and defense with quarterback LaNorris Sellers and edge rusher Dylan Stewart. When Sellers is on his game he is one of the best quarterbacks in the SEC, but he's been glaringly inconsistent. He had turnover problems in losses to Alabama and Mississippi State and was at that point tied for the second-worst completion rate in the SEC (62.1%). The next week he threw for 226 yards and two touchdowns with 147 rushing yards against Kentucky. Stewart has also had a season of ups and downs. He is a likely top-10 pick the 2027 NFL Draft but missed three of the first five games of this season, one because of a suspension after he punched an Alabama player in the helmet. Then he came back against Florida and dominated with two forced fumbles and a sack. If Sellers and Stewart are at their best, South Carolina can beat any team it plays. Tennessee's defense has been elite Few defenses in the country are as well-equipped as Tennessee's to handle a mobile quarterback like Sellers. The Vols rank first in the SEC in sacks, explosive plays allowed, tackles for loss, scoring defense, opposing passer rating and fourth-down defense. Defensive coordinator Jim Knowles' unit has been nothing short of dominant through seven games. The Vols have also forced multiple turnovers in three of their last four games, including four against Alabama. South Carolina lost the turnover battle in its first three SEC games and lost them all. When it was plus-three against Florida, it won by multiple scores. Tennessee vs South Carolina prediction Tennessee 24, South Carolina 21: This is a major trap game for Tennessee on the road after an emotional win, but its defense should travel just fine. The matchup may be decided by who's better between Vols running back DeSean Bishop and the Gamecocks' run defense that ranks third in the SEC. Oddsmakers slightly favor South Carolina in a spot that feels ripe for an unranked-over-ranked result. Still, picking against Tennessee's defense has been a fool's errand. Emmett Siegel covers Tennessee baseball for Knox News. Email: emmett.siegel@knoxnews.com ; X: @EmmettSiegel_

Tennessee is set to take on South Carolina on Saturday in Columbia. The Vols are coming off an emotional win over Alabama. And that win over Alabama combined with Tennessee's poor track record in Williams-Brice Stadium (UT is 2-6 in its last eight games in Columbia) has led to the Vols being put on upset alert this weekend by, well, almost everyone. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, picked South Carolina to beat Tennessee 27-24 . Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray, who is also an ESPN analyst, is making a similar prediction. Murray has South Carolina beating Tennessee 24-21. “So it comes down to picking this football game,” said Murray. “I really don't want to do this. I wish I could just not do it, but I've got to. South Carolina 24, Tennessee 21. I'm doing it because I love both teams. And what have we learned this year? Teams coming off an emotional win do not perform well the next week. Tennessee's coming off an emotional win. South Carolina's coming off a bye. The game is in South Carolina. You fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. We've been doing this all year. It feels like every big time game in college football, the winner loses the next week — especially if it's on the road.” “I love both teams,” added Murray. “… I'm just going with what history has told us this season. Tennessee had an emotional win against Bama. Smoking those cigars all night does not bode well for [recovery] the next day. So they're going on the road. South Carolina's healthy and coming off the bye. South Carolina wins.” I'm sure there will be some analysts here and there who pick Tennessee to win this game, but it seems like the majority of folks are picking South Carolina to come out on top. Tennessee has a big concern that's quietly developing and no one's talking about it, but it could be a big problem by the end of the season Josh Heupel and the Tennessee Volunteers have a potential problem quietly developing this season. Beamer has spoken with a level of concern regarding Scott’s injury, which caused him to spend some time in the hospital after the Kentucky game. He is listed as questionable on the injury report that was released Wednesday. It would be a huge blow if Johnson is unavailable to play. The Wildcats have dealt with injuries at the backup quarterback spot all season. Jacob Knuth, Blake Barnett and Dillon Duff have all dealt with injuries. After the early two losses, the Wildcats have limited margin for error the remainder of the season. And keeping Johnson healthy will be a key part of that happening. A three-year starter, Johnson is in the middle of perhaps his best collegiate season. He has completed 118 of 187 passes for 1,301 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Last week he had a huge day in the victory against the Kansas Jayhawks. He completed 14 of 24 passes for 209 yards and a touchdown. He also had 132 yards rushing on 12 carries in the 35-24 victory against the Jayhawks. The Wildcats could use Johnson in a game they hope can continue to build momentum this season. After a two-game losing streak (against the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars) to start the Big 12 schedule, they bounced back with a big victory against Kansas. A win against the Sun Devils would give the Wildcats a two-game winning streak in the conference. It would also keep them in the race for the Big 12 title game and a berth in the College Football Playoff. All of the signs are pointing toward Johnson playing this weekend in Tempe. The Wildcats coaching staff is likely just being cautious about his status. So expect him in uniform for Saturday's game If not, things could get dicey for the Wildcats. None of the backups have any real experience. It will be even tougher considering they are playing on the road against a conference rival. The hope is Johnson is ready to go to help the Wildcats' chance of moving three games ahead of .500.

away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. picks.blurb: That's the mantra of Clemson coach Dabo Swinney , whose teams sits at 4-2 and 2-1 in the ACC. The Tigers host the Virginia Tech Hokies (5-2, 2-2) in a critical prime-time matchup in Week 8 at Clemson Memorial Stadium. Clemson defeated Charleston Southern, 37-0, in Week 7 behind a defense that yielded only 76 yards of total offense and a rushing attack that ran for 231 yards. Chris Johnson Jr. had two touchdowns, and Gideon Davidson led the Tigers' ground game with 59 yards on 13 carries. Tigers receivers hurt themselves with some costly drops in the game, which is something Swinney has repeatedly highlighted this week . Quarterback Tait Reynolds finished 17 of 26 for 127 passing yards in the true freshman's fourth start at quarterback. Virginia Tech is coming off a 34-24 win over Georgia Tech in Blacksburg. Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns in the win. He leads the ACC in passing yards with 1,984 through seven games. Hokies leading rusher Jeffrey Overton is averaging six yards per carry. Coach James Franklin's team ranks 28th nationally in total offense, good for sixth in the ACC. The Hokies are 32nd nationally in total defense, fifth-best in the conference. Clemson is 110th nationally in total offense with 340.7 yards per game, second to last among ACC teams and ahead of only North Carolina. The Tigers are 46th nationally in total defense, which ranks 10th in the ACC. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Virginia Tech, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Hokies winning by three points, which goes against oddsmakers' 2.5 spread favoring the Tigers. Connelly's final score prediction: Virginia Tech 26, Clemson 23. He gives the Hokies a win probability of 56%. Where Clemson football sits in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 8 Clemson is No. 56 in the ESPN SP+ team rankings , up five spots from last week. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.0, up from 2.2 a week ago. Clemson is one spot below ACC rival Florida State (4.9) and one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.1 rating on offense (No. 98 nationally, down one spot from last week) and a 19.5 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is up five spots from before the Tigers' win over Charleston Southern. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.3 rating, which ranks 20th in the nation. Virginia Tech is No. 40 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 8.9, one spot below the Oregon State Beavers and one spot ahead of the Baylor Bears. The metrics give the Hokies a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 36 nationally, a 23.4 rating on defense that's No. 43 in the nation, and a minus-0.3 rating in special teams (No. 112). What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. 4 bold Virginia Tech predictions for Saturday night's primetime showdown at Clemson
picks.blurb: After breaking a two-game losing streak at home with a win over Georgia Tech last weekend, the Virginia Tech football team will hit the road this Saturday night for a key ACC battle at Clemson in a battle between a pair of two-loss teams. It'll be the first of three difficult road games remaining on the schedule in James Franklin's first season in Blacksburg. The Hokies will have home games next month, with Stanford and Virginia sprinkled in. Here are four bold predictions for Virginia Tech's primetime showdown in Death Valley. 4 Bold Virginia Tech football predictions for Clemson primetime showdown Virginia Tech scores 20-plus points This could end up being a low-scoring game, and some Clemson fans believe that the Tigers need to keep the Hokies under 20 points to have a realistic shot at winning. Virginia Tech has scored at least 20 points in every game this season, and Clemson has a stout defense. However, you have to think that Virginia Tech finds a way to break the 20-point plateau. It might not seem like a bit of a bold prediction, but the way the Tigers play defense and being on the road under the lights at Memorial Stadium, it is. Virginia Tech's defense forces multiple turnovers You have to think that Brent Pry's defense will build off of getting two takeaways last week against the Yellow Jackets and get multiple turnovers this week. If they want to have a shot at pulling off the upset, they will have to. Clemson's offense has sputtered at times this season, and getting off the field with some turnovers would go a long way toward securing an upset on the road. Turnovers both ways are going to play a big part in the outcome. Luke Reynolds records another 100 yards plus receiving Clemson coach Dabo Swinney spoke this week about Hokies tight end Luke Reynolds and how good he is. He got an up-close look at him last season in the Pinstripe Bowl when Penn State defeated the Tigers at Yankee Stadium. Clemson is going to know where Reynolds is on the field and look to shut him down, but that doesn't mean they will. Look for Hokies offensive coordinator Ty Howle to get him targets and for the future NFL tight end to make some big catches. Davion Brown records a touchdown reception Swinney spoke very highly of Reynolds and wide receiver/punt returner Que'Sean Brown this week, and it wouldn't be surprising to see the Tigers focus on them. While we believe that Reynolds will still have a big game, if they focus too much on Que'Sean Brown, that opens things up for freshman Davion Brown, and don't be surprised to see quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer target him a little more often. He made an outstanding one-handed catch against Georgia Tech last week and should see more balls thrown his way this weekend. Virginia Tech will need a wide receiver or two to step up, especially if the running game struggles. away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. away.blurb: News Sports Business Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? Drew Landon Clemson Wire Oct. 22, 2026, 6:30 a.m. CT Clemson football's initial availability report carries 10 injuries, one being fresh. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice. away.blurb: The Yellow Jackets are going to be trying to pull off an upset against the Hokies today, but they are going to have to do so with some key players out. The final availability report is out for this game, and it includes the final status for running back Justice Haynes, who was listed as doubtful coming into Saturday, as well as offensive lineman Josh Petty and defensive lineman Landen Marshall. RB Justice Haynes and OT Josh Petty are going to be game-time decisions. If Haynes is unable to go today, Trelain Maddox and Chad Alexander would be the top options in the backfield for the Yellow Jackets today against Virginia Tech. Maddox is coming off the best game of his career last week against Duke. Riggs, the Yellow Jackets starting center, came back from an injury last week in the win over Duke, but was hurt during the game and did not return. He was not on the injury report this week and should be starting in the middle of the Yellow Jackets offensive line against what has been one of the ACC's best defensive fronts through the first part of the season. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/georgiatech as Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets? . Kickoff time is getting closer for Georgia Tech and Virginia Tech. How do these injuries impact Georgia Tech today? There are two notable names not on the injury report this week and those are Jameson Riggs and Noah Carter. Carter has been perhaps the Yellow Jackets' most consistent pass rusher (although the pass rush has not been very good), and without Walker, Boyd, or Hoffler to get after the quarterback, Carter is going to be relied on to put pressure on Hokies QB Ethan Grunkemeyer, and Virginia Tech's offensive line has not been one of the best in the ACC so far this season. As poorly as the season started for Georgia Tech, a win on the road against the Hokies would be something that could potentially start to turn their season around. The Yellow Jackets have only one conference loss and with the ACC looking wide open after Miami, Georgia Tech can star to build some momentum that could get them to their fourth consecutive bowl appearance under Brent Key. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice. home.blurb: Starting Virginia Tech cornerback Thomas Williams is listed as questionable on the initial injury report for Clemson football's Week 8 ACC game against the Hokies . The initial report was released on Oct. 21. Cam Chadwick Jr., listed as a backup cornerback on the Hokies' depth chart, is also on the injury report as probable. On Clemson 's end, wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. home.headline: Virginia Tech Week 8 Availability Report: Latest Updates Ahead of Clemson Matchup
home.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Virginia Tech Week 8 Availability Report: Latest Updates Ahead of Clemson Matchup Skip to main content SI.COM More from Virginia Tech Hokies On SI FOOTBALL Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: WR Shamarius "Snook" Peterkin Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. Gordon Sellars III's injury may complicate Clemson's passing attack vs. Virginia Tech
home.blurb: The first ACC availability report for Virginia Tech at Clemson presents another challenge for the Tigers to sort out. Chad Morris will not have freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III available for this contest. He is working his way back from a concussion he recently suffered. Although Sellars only has three catches for eight yards on the season, he is a key depth piece in this receiving corps. While the initial injury report does give positive signs toward defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green returning, it may be more about Clemson finding ways to move the sticks aerially on this Virginia Tech defense than anything. Even if Christian Bentancur could be emerging at tight end, any player Tait Reynolds is comfortable with not being available is concerning for Clemson. Only major change for Clemson is freshman WR Gordon Sellars III (concussion) being out, which Dabo Swinney mentioned earlier tonight. Depth guys like Devarrick Woods (DT) and Jarvis Green (RB) aren't listed, indicating they'll be available to play https://t.co/d6ai25JL48 What Sellars' injury tells us coming in is that Clemson will now have one less role player available to potentially reignite a spark in this offense . This is the job Morris was hired to do. However, he can only make do with the players on this roster he inherited. Clemson just does not have the depth on the offensive side of the ball as it should. While Sellars was starting to come into his own, it is a setback. What Morris needs to do is go back to the drawing board to figure out ways he can inject any sort of explosiveness into this offense. Whether it be Johnson or Gideon Davidson out of the backfield, or really anyone in the passing game, Clemson needs to develop an ability to score points quickly in a hurry. It has been their biggest bugaboo all season long. Sellars could have been part of the solution. Sellars being out indicates that Morris must get even more creative with his offensive game planning. This is the part of the game where the Hokies are most vulnerable . While Clemson can play great defense, outstanding special teams, and occasionally look the part with the ground game, not having a reliable passing game could unravel the Tigers in the end. A third loss on the season would be incredibly devastating. Chad Morris must find ways to get the ball into his playmakers' hands The frustrating part is Clemson needed more than only the tight end wrinkle to unfurl in last week's win over Charleston Southern. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Arch Manning (16) leads Texas against Ole Miss and Trinidad Chambliss (6). For the first time in over a decade, Texas and Ole Miss meet on Saturday at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, at 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Longhorns are 3.5-point home favorites, and despite back-to-back losses, my Ole Miss vs. Texas prediction and college football picks project Arch Manning to pull off a win against his namesake's alma mater. TOP PICK Who will win Ole Miss vs Texas: Texas -3.5 Archie Manning never played against Texas, but Arch Manning has the chance to lead the Longhorns to their first win against his grandfather and uncle's alma mater since 2012. It's a good time to buy low on a Texas team I would take to cover up to -5.5 at home against Ole Miss . While the Longhorns have lost two straight, they still have the clear defensive advantage, even with Colin Simmons unlikely to play. The Texas defense ranks sixth nationally in available yards percentage (31.2%) and 14th in havoc rate (20%). Meanwhile, the Ole Miss defense struggled in ranked matchups away from home, allowing 90 points across two games. It's a big ask for Trinidad Chambliss to make up for his own defense again against one of the top defenses in the country. Chambliss is coming off arguably his worst game of the season, too (80.4 QBR, 65.7% adjusted completion percentage vs. Missouri ). Ole Miss vs Texas Over/Under pick: Over 53.5 While Texas' defensive advantage should make the difference in a Longhorns win, I'm expecting enough points to be scored for the Over to hit at 54.5 or better . The Ole Miss defense ranks 65th nationally in success rate (43.5%) and 89th in net EPA per drive, while allowing the most yards per game in the SEC (390). It's been at its worst away from home, allowing 35.6 points per game outside Oxford , helping the Over in all three of those games. But the Rebels have arguably the best QB in the country in Chambliss, who ranks top 20 in QBR (83.4) and TD passes (14). He and Kewan Lacy should move Ole Miss' offense with enough consistency for the Over to hit. I like Texas to win 31-24. Ole Miss vs Texas prop: Texas TT Over 27.5 While Pete Golding is a defensive coach, his team's defense has been sporadic at best this season. In four games against ranked opponents, Ole Miss is allowing 29.2 points per game, which is why I like Texas' team total Over at 28.5 or better . Ole Miss' defense ranks outside the top 75 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and early-down EPA per play. It's really struggled away from Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, allowing 38+ points and over 460 yards in two of its three games away from home . The biggest issue for Ole Miss is stopping the run. The Rebels have allowed the most rushing yards per game in the SEC (153.5). That should help Steve Sarkisian take pressure off Manning by leaning on his running backs. Ole Miss vs Texas combo This is the No. 2 must-watch game in my Top 25 predictions for Week 8, with Manning and Sarkisian looking for redemption and needing to cool down their seats. While Chambliss is my midseason first-team All-American QB, Ole Miss can't keep getting away with relying on him to carry it to wins... allowing 29.2 points per game against ranked teams will catch up to the Rebels. Without Simmons, this Texas defense will take a step back, but not a big enough step for Ole Miss to light it up and make up for its own defensive woes. Games away from home have been unkind to the Rebels, especially their defense, and I think Maning, Sarkisian, and the Longhorns offense will rise to the occasion to take advantage. The No. 7 Rebels boast a Heisman Trophy candidate in quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , and they've beaten three ranked teams behind a dynamic offense and a rock-solid defense. Texas has to face three ranked teams in its final six games of the regular season as well as two old rivals in Arkansas and Texas A&M. If the Longhorns want to remain in contention for a spot in the College Football Playoff, they'll have to beat Ole Miss . Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Ole Miss Rebels. No. 19 Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) vs. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) When: 6:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: The weather won't be as crisp as last week, but temperatures will still be in the low 80s at kickoff and dip into the 60s by the fourth quarter. Clear skies, full hearts for football fans. MORE: Fans turning on you is one thing, but former Texas players, too?
