Over/under : 53½ Texas history: Ole Miss All-time: Texas leads 6-2 Last meeting: Ole Miss 44, Texas 23 (Sept. 14, 2013) Most memorable meeting: Texas 12, Ole Miss 7 (1962). In a top-5 meeting that capped the 1961 regular season, the Longhorns held on for a hard-fought 12-7 win in the Cotton Bowl. The favored Rebels outgained Texas in yardage, 319-183, but the Longhorns had three interceptions, including three by Jerry Cook. For fifth-year coach Darrell Royal, the victory gave him his first 10-win season at Texas as well as his first bowl triumph. Royal would go on to six more 10-win seasons and seven more bowl wins at Texas before retiring after the 1976 season. MORE: Steve Sarkisian evaluated 'everything' after Texas football loss. Are changes coming? Know the foe: Ole Miss Last week: Beat Missouri, 31-3 Players to watch: QB Trinidad Chambliss , a 6-foot-1, 205-pound senior, won a court battle with the NCAA in the offseason for a sixth year of eligibility. He's beating plenty of defenses, too; he ranks second in the SEC with 279.3 yards passing per game and has accounted for 20 total touchdowns. RB Kewan Lacey , a 5-11, 205-pound junior from the Dallas suburb of Lancaster, earned all-SEC accolades last season but has battled injuries while carrying the ball 62 times for 352 yards and five touchdowns this season. But he looked plenty healthy last week with a season-high 122 yards against Missouri. LB Suntarine Perkins, a 6-2, 220-pound senior, is off to a quiet start with just 20 tackles and 1½ sacks. But he has 21 sacks in his career, and he's the twitchy kind of edge rusher that has given the Texas line fits this season. Central Texas connections: Freshman quarterback Reese Wise hasn't played this season but boasts some pedigree considering he comes from the quarterback factory at Westlake High School.… Former blue-chip receiver recruit Johntay Cook II signed with Texas in 2023 and appeared in 20 games over two seasons for the Longhorns before transferring to Syracuse. Now in his first season at Ole Miss, he has just one catch for -3 yards. When Texas has the ball Could Raleek Brown be the workhorse this week? He looks like the only healthy back since freshman Derrek Cooper missed last week's game with an undisclosed injury and Hollywood Smothers missed practice earlier in the week with a reported arm or shoulder injury. Brown did rip off a 32-yard run against Florida but had just 15 yards on seven other carries. Ole Miss held Missouri to 39 yards on 26 carries behind a dominant effort from DT Will Echoles, and the Texas offensive line has struggled in short-yardage situations against Oklahoma and Florida. Quarterback Arch Manning talks about "letting it rip," but the fourth-year quarterback has struggled this season while averaging only 215.8 yards a game on 63.9% passing. Ole Miss ranks just 11 th in the SEC in pass defense with 233.3 yards allowed per game, and Missouri's Donovan Olugbode exploded for nine catches and 128 yards. High-paid Auburn transfer Cam Coleman (20 catches, 336 yards, 6 TDs) will try and do the same. MORE: Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning fight for blame in Texas football's offensive struggles When Ole Miss has the ball Texas may have to play without All-American edge rusher Colin Simmons , who leads the nation with 10 ½ sacks but will likely miss the game with a reported ankle injury. Tackle Maraad Waston (three sacks) is the only other Longhorn with more than one sack, which is bad news against an Ole Miss offensive line that has allowed an SEC-low five sacks all season. The Rebels only trail Georgia when it comes to yards per carry in the SEC with an impressive 5.15 in league play, but they've also run it just a league-low 190 times in all games. Texas allows a league-low 103.7 yards rushing a game in SEC play, which means Chambliss could air it out more than usual to a receiving corps led by Deuce Alexander (19 catches, 275 yards). Texas running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs the ball during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Ole Miss key matchup Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles vs. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. With Simmons likely out for the game, Rasheem Biles needs to step up as a playmaker after going three straight games without a takeaway or a forced fumble. And he'll have to do it while keeping an eye on the slippery Chambliss, who has rushed for 127 yards this season. Texas vs Ole Miss prediction Thomas Jones: Ole Miss 28, Texas 24. The Longhorns' offense has its best game in league play, but the expected absence of Simmons is too much to overcome against arguably the top quarterback in the nation. Danny Davis: Texas. I feel like this is a version of the Anakin Skywalker meme where Padmé asks "There is no way that the Longhorns' football season essentially ends before Halloween, right?," gets a blank stare from Anakin and then has to desperately state the question again. Texas wins this game for no other reason than it has to. Michael Shapiro: Ole Miss 28, Texas 27 . This is a perfect emotional spot for the Longhorns, who will take the field with plenty of fire with their backs against the wall. I still can't shake the matchup concerns. Ole Miss has perhaps the best quarterback in college football in Trinidad Chambliss. Texas will be without edge rusher Colin Simmons, perhaps college football's best defensive player. Add in the defensive chops of Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding, and a bounce-back for Texas is no guarantee. picks.headline: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch
picks.blurb: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning warms up before a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. © Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Prateek Singh Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:41 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Arch Manning's struggles against the Florida Gators have put the Texas Longhorns in a difficult position ahead of their matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday. Manning threw for 173 yards, completed 14 of 20 passes, and threw one touchdown. According to former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel, Texas will need to make key adjustments to its strategy ahead of the upcoming game. During an appearance on CBS Sports, Neuheisel picked Ole Miss to win. "I'm concerned for Texas in this game, not because I don't think they'll play hard and be geared up to play their best game of the season, but I feel like because of all the pressure on Arch, they're going to condense, and condensing will not be the answer to going against Pete Golding defense," he said . Neuheisel pointed out that Arch Manning attempted just 20 passes against Florida, arguing that such an approach will not be effective against the Ole Miss Rebels. While the Texas Longhorns have won four of their six games this season, Manning has shown only flashes of brilliance rather than the consistency expected of him. Overall, Manning has completed 106 of 166 passes for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns, and five interceptions. After his performance against the Gators, speculation began that he could be benched for the upcoming game. However, head coach Steve Sarkisian made it clear that Arch Manning will remain the team's starting quarterback. "There's no doubt about it, Arch can play better for us, but he's our starter," he said , per Fox Sports. "We need to see a better version of him this week." Sarkisian said Manning is a quality player and that, as a coach, it is his job to bring out the best in him on the field. Former Texas Coach Heaps Praise on Arch Manning On an episode of THE STAMPEDE, former Texas coach Mack Brown said Arch Manning and the rest of the Longhorns are playing under immense pressure. He believes the team needs to free itself from that pressure before stepping onto the field. In Brown's view, Manning has the talent and ability to help get Texas back on track. "Arch's gotta go back and be the Arch we saw at the last of last year," he said. "He's good enough, he's athletic enough, he's smart enough, and for a 22-year-old, he has handled this pressure so well." Brown said the upcoming matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels will be crucial for the Longhorns and could shape their chances of making the College Football Playoff this season. picks.blurb: College Football Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football If not for one single step, last week's picks would have been dominant. But college football sometimes works like that. One minute you're breaking free of the defensive back, eyeing a walk-off win in one of the biggest games of the year. The next, your foot inexplicably lands out of bounds, and everything goes up in flames. It was that close for Indiana last week against Ohio State. We were also that close to a 7-2 week, although 6-3 will do just fine. As for Week 8, consider us intrigued. It doesn't have the same buffet of massive matchups on paper, although those are normally the weeks that deliver. After such a bananas Saturday, maybe it's just going to be one of those seasons. Here's to hoping. As for another week of winners, here they are. Last Week's Record: 6-3 Year to Date: 33-33-1 All point spreads courtesy of FanDuel Texas (-3) vs. Ole Miss Tim Warner/Getty Images Oh, it's a mess in Austin. Let's not paint this picture any differently. Following an emphatic come-from-behind win over Ohio State, Texas played a lackluster game against UTSA and followed it up with two ugly losses to Oklahoma and Florida. Steve Sarkisian spent a week defending Arch Manning; now he's giving backup quarterback KJ Lacey Jr., who has thrown a grand total of nine passes across his two seasons with the program, more reps. Despite the losses and the drama, Texas is favored over a team coming off (arguably) its best win all season. Ole Miss clobbered Missouri, which was playing fantastic football coming into last week. Perhaps most importantly, the Rebels limited the Mizzou offense to just three points. So, why do this? Why should we back a team in disarray despite all the recent data points? Beyond our general contrarian style, Ole Miss didn't exactly dazzle in its only true road test thus far against Florida, allowing the Gators to rack up nearly 500 yards of offense. While the Longhorns have issues in all facets, playing on the road in this conference is never easy. Texas, questions aplenty, finds a way. The Pick: Texas (-3) South Carolina (-2.5) vs. Tennessee James Gilbert/Getty Images From one fascinating point spread in the SEC to another, enter South Carolina-Tennessee. The Vols, currently. No. 11 in the AP Poll, coming off a dominant win over Alabama, are underdogs to a three-win team that suffered an ugly three-game losing streak earlier in the year. Such is life in the SEC. For Tennessee, what a performance from the defense. The Vols' D limited Alabama to just 201 yards of offense and forced four turnovers. Tennessee is currently No. 9 in scoring defense and first in the nation in sacks. The issue, however, is that the offense never looked quite right. QB George MacIntyre wasn't superb, but he did enough. While we might not know the starter until game day, it seems likely that MacIntyre will get the nod over Faizon Brandon. For South Carolina, it probably won't matter. In dire need of a win, the Gamecocks absolutely clobbered Florida in their last game before enjoying a bye in Week 7. LaNorris Sellers had arguably his best collegiate game to date. Dylan Stewart was back and all over the place. All was right for one week. Now, South Carolina will play at home against a team with massive hangover potential. The timing is right. The Pick: South Carolina (-2.5) Wisconsin (+3) vs. USC Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For Wisconsin, Week 7 was a missed opportunity. There's no other way to shape it. UCLA deserves credit for beating the Badgers with a backup QB, although Wisconsin had plenty of chances to win. Completing just six passes and throwing for 66 yards doesn't help. Despite the lack of offense, the oddsmakers see this as a tight game. USC, which enjoyed a bye last week, comes into Week 8 with a solid 6-1 mark. However, the reality behind those numbers tells a different story. USC played an ugly football game against Rutgers, lost to Oregon without its starting QB and nearly lost to Washington and Penn State. Lincoln Riley deserves credit for finding a way to win those games. That's one way to look at it. Another is that the Trojans are due for a slip-up. This feels like a moment that fits that outcome perfectly. Wisconsin must find a way to get quarterback Colton Joseph into a better rhythm. He should find success on the ground; that's the norm. But getting more comfortable as a passer should be the goal. Defensively, Wisconsin should slow USC's offense. If the Wisconsin offense can do enough, don't be shocked if the Badgers win outright. The Pick: Wisconsin (+3) Week 8 CFB Picks 🔮 Latest CFB Odds and Picks ✍️ B/R's Expert Week 7 NFL Picks 🔮 UCF (+6.5) vs. BYU Brian Bahr/Getty Images Well, we know how the public will bet this one. Coming off an enormous win over Notre Dame, BYU, which is now No. 2 in the AP Poll, is laying less than a touchdown against an unranked team with a .500 record. The masses will flock to bet BYU. In many ways, it makes sense. Quarterback Bear Bachmeier is excellent. BYU's defense just played a largely brilliant game. There's a lot to like about this program, as the development under Kalani Sitake is undeniable. But let's make sure our memories aren't short. This same BYU team struggled on the road against TCU and wasn't exactly dominant against Iowa State. That's not meant to take anything away from their efforts. It simply points out that these opponents have delivered close games before. While the Cougars will travel after an emphatic win, UCF enjoyed a bye after two consecutive losses on the road. Quarterback Keyone Jenkins has played well while filling in for starter Alonza Barnett III. He'll start again. At home, this team looks like it could push the No. 2 team to the brink. The oddsmakers feel that way, and so do we. The Pick: UCF (+6.5) Michigan (+7) vs. Indiana Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images Football hangovers work in mysterious ways, and we're about to find out exactly how Indiana responds after suffering a loss—something it hasn't done in quite some time. And it wasn't just any loss; this was a heartbreaker. Yes, Indiana could have beaten Ohio State if not for the play we alluded to at the very start. But to summarize the Hoosiers' performance on this play alone would be a mistake. Indiana's offense looked out of sync, Josh Hoover missed a lot of easy throws and the Hoosiers' running game averaged just two-and-a-half yards per carry, albeit against a quality opponent and defense. Michigan, meanwhile, has new life. Quarterback Bryce Underwood was benched for freshman Tommy Carr, grandson of Michigan legend Lloyd Carr. After entering the game, Carr led the Wolverines to a key win over Penn State. While head coach Kyle Whittingham didn't officially name Carr the starter, it feels like a formality. In terms of energy, this game features one team riding the high of its new starting QB playing at home. The other is trying to shake off the emotions of a really difficult loss. Indiana wins. Michigan keeps it tight. The Pick: Michigan (+7) Other Games on the Card Zach Del Bello/Getty Images Memphis (-10) vs. East Carolina The Tigers turned the ball over six times in an ugly loss against Tulane. They were still in the game for a while. Playing at home as a double-digit favorite should be exactly what this team needs. TCU (-9.5) vs. West Virginia Another sizable chalk, which feels somewhat noteworthy, given West Virginia's Week 7 win over Cincinnati at home. The Mountaineers won for us last week, although we still have serious concerns about that defense. Kansas (+3) vs Baylor The Baylor offense mustered just six points last week against TCU. The Bears are just a short favorite over a two-win team. It goes without saying, but Kansas could use this one badly. Nevada (-5.5) vs. San Jose State On the topic of backing two-win teams, enter Nevada. The schedule hasn't exactly been favorable of late, which is at least partly to blame. This week, the oddsmakers see things differently. As do we. Arizona State (+3.5) vs. Kansas State It didn't go well for Arizona State against Texas Tech. That's perhaps putting it mildly. picks.blurb: my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores SPORTS & TEAMS PERSONALITIES POPULAR SEARCHES College Football Add FOX Sports on Google College Football Week 8 Expert Picks, Predictions For Texas-Ole Miss And More Updated Oct. 22, 2026 1:01 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Week 7 of the college football season was chaotic, with five of the top seven teams falling. The upsets confounded experts everywhere, but they'll try to rebound in Week 8. It starts with "Big Noon Kickoff" as No. 6 Indiana tries to bounce back from its loss to No. 3 Ohio State against a Michigan team, resurging after a quarterback change. Arch Manning will try to keep his job as he leads No. 19 Texas into a must-win game against No. 7 Ole Miss. Then the night ends with a Big 12 matchup with College Football Playoff stakes when undefeated No. 10 Utah hosts No. 14 Houston. After consecutive weeks where the No. 1 team lost, the field is wide open. Weâre breaking down our straight-up picks and the matchups to watch closely throughout the weekend. Michigan vs. No. 6 Indiana Curt Cignetti and Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end when the Hoosiers were defeated by Ohio State in Week 7. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (FOX) Where: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, Michigan Line: Indiana -7 RJ Young: Indiana After watching Indiana's defense turn Julian Sayin into a tackling dummy, I shudder to think what it might do against Michigan's newly named starting quarterback, Tommy Carr. Laken Litman: Indiana The Hoosiers have never lost back-to-back games under Curt Cignetti and that won't start now â not even with Michigan likely starting Tommy Carr at quarterback. Ben Portnoy: Indiana After being in Bloomington last week for Indiana's loss to Ohio State, I think I'm more confident than ever that the Hoosiers can repeat as Big Ten champions. Michigan should get a nice spark from Tommy Carr, but I'm skeptical of a first-time starter against Bryant Haines' defense. No. 1 Miami vs. Pitt Quarterback Darian Mensah kept Miami's undefeated season alive with multiple clutch drives against Florida State. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (ESPN) Where: Hard Rock Stadium, Miami, Florida Line: Miami -20.5 Young: Miami The No. 1 team in the country needs to act like it against a team that lost its star player and starting quarterback Mason Heintschel earlier this season. Litman: Miami The 'Canes escaped their scariest test of the season vs. Florida State last week and will be locked in against a struggling Pitt team. Portnoy: Miami Pitt hasn't been the same team since Mason Heintschel was lost for the season. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is still my pick for the Heisman Trophy and I think he'll put up more big numbers on Saturday. No. 18 LSU vs. Auburn Alex Golesh led Auburn to an upset over top-ranked Georgia in Week 7, the first time the Tigers have defeated the No. 1 ranked team since 2017. (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (ABC) Where: Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn, Alabama Line: LSU -7.5 Young: LSU I sincerely doubt Auburn can pull off that trick of knocking off a top-25 team for the second week in a row. Litman: Auburn Jordan-Hare Stadium will be rocking and ready for Auburn to upset its second straight SEC powerhouse. Portnoy: LSU The Tigers are in do-or-die mode right now. LSU brass spent millions to flip this roster and bring Lane Kiffin to Baton Rouge. I think it keeps its CFP hopes â fleeting as they may be â alive for one more week. UCF vs. No. 2 BYU BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw for one touchdown and rushed for two more in the Cougars' upset of Notre Dame in Week 7. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FOX) Where: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, Florida Line: BYU -6.5 Young: BYU I don't believe in "emotional letdowns," and UCF has been playing without star quarterback Alonza Barnett III most of this season. Litman: BYU The Cougars don't seem like the kind of team that's going to have a letdown week after their massive win over Notre Dame. How many ways will quarterback Bear Bachmeier score this Saturday? Portnoy: BYU No Alonza Barnett III, no way UCF is winning this game. The Golden Knights have improved in Year 2 of the Scott Frost Era (Part 2), but the Cougars look like the best team in the Big 12. I think they get it done, even in a potential letdown spot here. South Carolina vs. No. 11 Tennessee Josh Heupel improved to 2-1 against Kalen DeBoer. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (ESPN) Where: Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia, South Carolina Line: South Carolina -2.5 Young: Tennessee With George MacIntyre at quarterback and DeSean Bishop as the engine powering the Power T offense, the Volunteers look a lot like the 2024 version that made the College Football Playoff. Litman: Tennessee It's never easy to win on the road in the SEC, but Tennessee ekes this one out against a rejuvenated South Carolina team coming off a bye. Portnoy: South Carolina Tennessee smoked Alabama last week, but I'm still not sure how good the Volunteers are. away.headline: Three Ole Miss offensive linemen on injury report, but there’s reason for optimism
away.blurb: Ole Miss has some personnel questions heading into Saturday night's showdown at Texas, but one part of Wednesday's SEC availability report stood out more than anything else. Three starting offensive linemen appeared on it. Starting left tackle Terez Davis and center Brycen Sanders were listed as questionable, while right guard Patrick Kutas was listed as probable. The good news for Ole Miss is there's no reason to believe any of the three are in serious danger of missing the game. Kutas, especially, would be a surprise absence given his probable designation. Sanders returned to last week's 31-3 win over Missouri after leaving with an injury, and while Davis didn't come back, he remained on the sideline in uniform. Still, it's hard to ignore seeing three starters from the same position group show up on the report before a road trip to Austin. The concern isn't necessarily whether they'll play. It's the fact Ole Miss is entering one of its biggest games of the season with questions along the offensive front. As for Kewan Lacy, his inclusion feels far less significant. Lacy was listed as probable after briefly leaving last week's game with a hamstring issue, but he still ran for 122 yards against Missouri. At this point, it wouldn't be surprising if his name appears on most injury reports the rest of the season as Ole Miss manages the situation. The bigger story remains the offensive line. If the Rebels have all three starters available Saturday night, they'll likely feel good about where they stand. But heading into a hostile road environment against a talented Texas defense, it's a group worth monitoring. Colin Simmons' absence would be a big break for Ole Miss While Ole Miss is watching the health of its offensive line, Texas appears likely to be without one of the nation's premier pass rushers. EDGE Colin Simmons was listed as doubtful after suffering an ankle sprain in last week's loss to Florida. That designation aligns with reports earlier this week indicating Simmons is expected to miss multiple weeks. Barring a surprising turnaround, it would be unexpected to see him on the field Saturday. That's significant for Ole Miss. Simmons leads the nation with 10.5 sacks and has been the centerpiece of the Texas pass rush. The Longhorns also listed EDGE Richard Wesley as out, further impacting their depth up front. Texas still has plenty of defensive talent, so this isn't a matchup-changing development by itself. But for an Ole Miss offensive line dealing with multiple injury concerns, potentially avoiding the nation's leading sacker is about as favorable a piece of injury news as the Rebels could have received this week. away.headline: Arch Manning's QB1 Status Updated by Steve Sarkisian Ahead of No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss
away.blurb: Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian came short Thursday of committing to Arch Manning as his starter past the No. 19 Longhorns' home game against No. 7 Ole Miss this Saturday. "It just depends," Sarkisian said about Manning's status in a Thursday Zoom call with reporters (h/t the Austin American-Statesman 's Michael Shapiro). "Every game's different. "I think Arch has had a good week of work. He's prepared himself well, but like the team, we need to play well. So, we'll go from there." Asked about Manning's attitude in the week leading up to the matchup, Sarkisian attributed what he described as the quarterback's edginess in part to media scrutiny of his struggles. "At some point he's gotta fight back," Sarkisian said about media coverage of Manning, per Shapiro . "The best way to fight back is playing good football with his teammates and enjoying playing good football with his teammates." Sarkisian also praised backup quarterback KJ Lacey ahead of Saturday's matchup. "KJ's a good player. He's dynamic with the ball in his hands. He's a natural passer," Sarkisian said, according to Inside Texas' Evan Vieth . Sarkisian added there were some "growing pains" in getting Lacey adjusted given his lack of prior playing time but that the four-star 2025 recruit was "coachable" and had "good rapport with his teammates," per Vieth. The latest comments from the Longhorns coach came after he said Monday that Texas would be sticking with their incumbent starter, but that he needed to see "a better version of Arch Manning" going forward (h/t OnTexas' CJ Vogel ). Sarkisian also said Monday that Lacey has been taking weekly first-team reps, per Vogel. Texas was ranked as the AP Poll's top team before conceding consecutive losses to Oklahoma and Florida. Manning's decision-making has repeatedly come into question over that stretch, which was capped off last Saturday by his costly fumble late in the fourth quarter against Florida. Manning, 22, has struggled with consistency throughout his second full season as Texas' starting quarterback. Whether he is able to show any progress in this weekend's matchup against Ole Miss could impact whether Sarkisian continues working on his development or considers turning to Lacey down the stretch of the season.

Whether he is able to show any progress in this weekend's matchup against Ole Miss could impact whether Sarkisian continues working on his development or considers turning to Lacey down the stretch of the season.

picks.headline: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week. picks.headline: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:38 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will try to keep to momentum rolling as they enter their bye week after they host Vanderbilt under the lights on Saturday. Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 22, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky Football looks to keep climbing after Oklahoma win as Vanderbilt comes to Lexington. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. picks.headline: How No. 12 Kentucky football and Vanderbilt match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 21 of 28 passes for 158 yards and two touchdowns in the Wildcats’ 21-13 win at Oklahoma last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound transfer from Notre Dame has been a paragon of efficiency so far as a Wildcat. On the season, Minchey has completed 68.4% of his throws for 1,551 yards with 13 touchdowns vs. one interception . • Vanderbilt true freshman Jared Curtis is a player UK coach Will Stein sought to recruit while serving as Oregon offensive coordinator. “He’s very young,” Stein said of Curtis, “but in terms of the tangibles of the position, being able to throw it, arm talent, running strength, he is a prototype first-round-type talent.” A homegrown, 6-3, 230-pound Nashville product, Curtis is completing 62.7% of his throws for 1,242 yards and six touchdowns. Ball security has been an issue for the freshman QB, who has thrown seven interceptions and lost two fumbles. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky leading rusher CJ Baxter (484 yards, 5.6 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) sat out last week’s victory at Oklahoma with an undisclosed injury. In Baxter’s absence, third-year player Jason Patterson led UK with 38 yards on 12 carries vs. the Sooners. Former Oklahoma back Jovantae Barnes carried five times for 16 yards last week vs. his former team. • Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea deploys a two-man running back rotation. Senior Sedrick Alexander has run for 270 yards and five touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards a rush. The 5-9, 207-pound product of Austin, Texas, has also caught 11 passes for 94 yards and a score. Senior Makhilyn Young has rushed for 232 yards and two TDs and is averaging 4.2 yards a carry. A 5-10, 210-pound product of Midland, Texas, Young has caught 10 passes for 76 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby was named a Midseason Freshman All-American by On3 Sports this week. The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, leads UK with 34 catches and 436 receiving yards and is tied for the team lead with three touchdown receptions. Senior Nic Anderson made an acrobatic, juggling catch against Oklahoma — the team for whom he played as a freshman. Over the past three games, the 6-4, 205-pound Atlanta product has caught 13 passes. On the season, Anderson has 17 catches for 197 yards and a TD. • Vanderbilt senior Junior Sherrill is fourth in the SEC in receptions with 41. A 5-11, 200-pound Nashville product, Sherrill has 628 receiving yards and has caught four touchdown passes. In Vandy’s 45-17 strafing of UK last season, Sherrill caught eight passes for 115 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is putting together an All-SEC-caliber season. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School caught five passes for 38 yards and two touchdowns in last week’s win at Oklahoma. On the season, Rodriguez has 33 catches for 257 yards and three TDs. • A transfer from East Carolina who began his college career at Ole Miss, Vanderbilt’s Jayvontay Conner has 13 catches for 146 yards. Cole Spence has six receptions for 72 yards. In last season’s blowout of UK, Spence caught three passes for 48 yards. Offensive line • Kentucky left offensive tackle Lance Heard was named a First Team Mid-Season All-American this week by On3 Sports. A 6-6, 325-pound product of Bonita, Louisiana, Heard was recently ranked the 29th-best prospect for the 2027 NFL draft by CBSSports.com. • Vanderbilt “quick guard” Cade McConnell is the only returning starter along the offensive front from last season’s 10-3 team. A 6-5, 323-pound product of Choctaw, Oklahoma, McConnell began his college career at Minnesota. Center Lyndon Cooper logged 25 career starts at Pittsburgh and was considered a portal-recruiting coup for Vandy. Advantage: Kentucky Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace and tackle Tavion Gadson were disruptive forces for UK late in the win at Oklahoma. Humphrey-Grace, a 6-4, 271-pound senior from Cincinnati, was credited with 1.5 sacks and three quarterback hurries vs. the Sooners. It was Humphrey-Grace deflecting the ball off the throwing hand of Oklahoma QB John Mateer that set up the Ty Bryant interception that was the turning point in the game. Gadson, a 6-5, 303-pound junior from Savannah, Georgia, made eight tackles, 1.5 sacks and broke up a pass. “Those guys are really good players,” Will Stein said of Gadson and Humphrey-Grace. • At 6-7, 305 pounds, Vanderbilt tackle Issa Ouattara is an impactful presence in the interior of the Commodores’ defensive front. A product of Cologne, Germany, Ouattara has two sacks and three QB hurries so far in 2026. Edge Miles Capers leads Vandy with six tackles for loss and has two sacks, an interception and the forced fumble that set up Vanderbilt’s game-winning touchdown on the final play of a 35-31 victory over North Carolina State. • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey made a game-high 15 tackles at Oklahoma. WLB Bo Barnes was not far behind with 10 stops. It has been a season of starts and stops for fifth-year player Alex Afari . The 6-2, 227-pound Cincinnati product is a member of the high school class of 2022 that the NCAA has attempted to exclude from the new 5-for-5 eligibility model. Afari was eligible for UK’s first four games due to a ruling in Jefferson County Circuit Court. However, the NCAA won on appeal at the Kentucky Court of Appeals, making Afari ineligible for the South Carolina and LSU games. A subsequent ruling by the Jefferson County Circuit Court last week restored Afari’s eligibility prior to the Oklahoma contest. The legal back-and-forth “is frustrating for him and for us,” Will Stein said. “We just got to roll with the punches a little bit. It’s out of our control. It’s out of his control at the end of the day, and he’s responded appropriately.” • Vanderbilt WLB Nick Rinaldi is a stat stuffer. A 6-3, 240-pound product of Dover, Massachusetts, Rinaldi has made 42 tackles, 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks and has hurried the quarterback four times and broken up passes four times. MLB Bryan Longwell is second on the team with 50 tackles. Longwell had a TFL in Vandy’s rout of UK last season. Advantage : Vanderbilt Defensive backs • Kentucky senior safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell each had two interceptions in the win over Oklahoma. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound transfer from Florida, foiled a Sooners’ fake field goal with an interception in the end zone and later returned a pick of John Mateer 41 yards for the game’s final touchdown. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Frederick Douglass High School alumnus, set up Kentucky’s go-ahead TD with a 42-yard interception return, then sealed the Wildcats’ victory with a pick with 21 seconds left in the game. • Vanderbilt strong safety CJ Heard leads the Commodores in tackles with 52. A 5-11, 210-pound Atlanta product who began his college career at Florida Atlantic, Heard also has made four tackles for loss, three sacks, broken up five passes, forced two fumbles and intercepted a pass. Special teams • Kentucky has not had consistently stellar punting in 2026, but Wilson Berry played a big role in the win at Oklahoma. The Australian uncorked a 58-yard, rugby-style kick that backed OU up to its 4-yard line with 2:43 left in the game. On the season, Berry is averaging 44 yards on eight punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 8 of 11 on field goals in 2026 with a long make of 52 yards. • Vanderbilt punter Tyler Ebel is averaging 47 yards a kick and has pinned opponents inside their 20-yard line on 10 of 27 punts. Place-kicker Brock Taylor is 6 of 8 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 47 yards. For his college career, Taylor is 47 of 53 on field-goal tries with a long make of 57 yards. away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. home.blurb: For Kentucky, linebacker Sam Greene is a significant one to monitor, as he is listed as doubtful. Receiver Nic Anderson is also questionable. Linebacker Grant Grayton is once again listed as out for Saturday's game. Will Stein does not expect it to be a season-long issue. “Not expected to be a season thing, so I'm hoping over the next few weeks we can get him back." The Wildcats will likely get CJ Baxter back ahead of Saturday's matchup, as he is listed as probable, along with linebacker Tavion Wallace. Kentucky football has been pretty banged up on the defensive end lately and were also without starting running back CJ Baxter this past Saturday against Oklahoma. After picking up a gritty win down in Norman, the Wildcats will be taking on a Vandy team that is winless in the SEC through four games, but one that Kentucky can't overlook. As the Wildcats continue to pop up in many playoff projections after yet another win, every single day becomes important if they want to capitalize on a historic start through seven games. Ahead of the matchup with Vandy, here is what the injury report looks like. Earlier this week, Stein made sure his players and fans know to not underestimate what Vandy can do. He isn't paying attention to that 3-4 record next to their name. "I don't think any of us in this room or this organization need to be fooled by any type of record. Last time I checked, (Vandy) embarrassed Kentucky last year and so we know what they are able to do in all three phases." Vandy also features one of the best wide receivers in the country, who is 11th nationally in receiving yards and a massive focal point in how they find success on offense. That, along with Kentucky needing to continue winning to keep their playoff hopes alive are the stories entering this one. The Wildcats can't afford a slip up ahead of a tough stretch to end the season. They'll be facing Vandy mostly healthy on Saturday. What does Kentucky football have to do to achieve its postseason dreams? picks.blurb: Pick yourself back up because the opening Wisconsin vs. USC odds will look familiar Skip to main content About Us Wisconsin Badgers News Wisconsin Football Wisconsin Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Wisconsin Badgers In The Pros Wisconsin Football Recruiting Wisconsin Football All-Time Lists Wisconsin Basketball Recruiting Wisconsin Women's Basketball Wisconsin Basketball All-Time Lists The Wisconsin Badgers suffered an incredibly frustrating loss against the UCLA Bruins on the road this weekend. You can be mad at the officials for a bunch of bad or missed calls; you can shout at the offense for only scoring seven points; at Colton Joseph for only managing 66 passing yards; or even at the defense for being miserable on third downs. But wallow for a bit, reset, pick yourself up, and let's look at the upcoming game on Saturday. The Badgers get another primetime game on NBC against another Los Angeles school. Wisconsin takes on the USC Trojans, and the odds have dropped; and they may look eerily familiar. Wisconsin vs. USC odds, spread and total Odds provided by FanDuel Sportsbook Wisconsin +112 Wisconsin +2.5 (-108) USC -2.5 (+112) 48.5 (over -114/under -106) Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Wisconsin goes into another game in which they are less than three-point underdogs. This is how the line ended last week against UCLA. It may have started around 4.5 or 3.5, depending on which book you looked at, but it ended at 2.5. So, Wisconsin is staring down a very similar outlook to UCLA in terms of Vegas predictions. There is a major difference between the two odds... the over/under looks a lot different. Wisconsin vs. UCLA was at low odds around 43.5, but now it's getting higher. Not drastically higher, but it jumped up to 48.5 as a total score. That may surprise you, considering Wisconsin only scored 7 points last week against the Bruins. But UCLA has a stout defense; the Trojans have holes in theirs. They've only lost one game this season, but it wasn't because of the defense. The Trojan defense has allowed 20+ points in six of their seven games. USC wins because they have also averaged 36.4 points a game. So, Vegas is saying, Wisconsin will certainly score more against the Trojans and we can assume USC will also score against Wisconsin but low enoguh that it won't be that high scoring. An over/under of 48.5 with only a 2.5 spread predicts the final score to be somewhere around 26-23. It's an interesting matchup for Vegas to predict because USC's strength is the offense and their weakness is their defense. You can basically flip that for Wisconsin, whose defense has been pretty spectacular this season, especially when it comes to scoring defense. But the offense has been rocky at best and putrid at worst. So, the odds feel interesting but pretty close to what you would predict, especially with Wisconsin being the home team and getting to host the USC Trojans. away.blurb: After the injury update that Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin will be out indefinitely, the competition for the starting position has begun between Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair. The Buckeyes have time to decide, as they are currently on a bye week following their 19-15 road win over the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers in Bloomington. When the No. 16 USC Trojans take the field for one of their most important games of the season against the No. 3 Ohio State Buckeyes at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Halloween night, one of the major questions is who they'll face at quarterback. Fahey starting for the Buckeyes against the Trojans on Oct. 31 would be a storyline in itself, as he's a former three-star recruit from Mission Viejo, California, which is on the border of the Los Angeles metropolitan area. St. Clair also has a strong case to start, as he's a former five-star recruit from Bellefontaine, Ohio. Sayin’s injury impacts the Big Ten title and College Football Playoff race, and one conference team could benefit from the loss. That team is the No. 16 USC Trojans, whom the Buckeyes will face at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum after their bye week. Depending on Saturday's road result against the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium, a win over the Buckeyes will boost the Trojans' Big Ten title and CFP chances in their fifth season under coach Lincoln Riley. How Julian Sayin's Affects USC Trojans The Trojans (6-1 overall, 3-1 Big Ten) look to beat the Buckeyes without Sayin and give Riley his biggest win at USC. Facing the Buckeyes without Sayin gives the Trojans an advantage, and falling short at home against an Ohio State team without its leading signal caller would be a huge missed opportunity for Riley’s team. Despite Sayin’s absence, several Buckeyes on the roster will challenge the Trojans' defense, which has seen its fair share of ups and downs in its first season under defensive coordinator Gary Patterson. How Ohio State Can Still Beat USC Without Sayin The country's best wide receiver and Heisman Trophy frontrunner, Jeremiah Smith, is one of those players looking to lead the Buckeyes to a win over the Trojans without Sayin. The Buckeyes star, with a backup quarterback under center, will look to make key plays against a struggling Trojans secondary. In seven games this season, Smith has recorded 52 receptions for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns. Smith is second in the country in receiving behind Oregon State Beavers wide receiver Jesse Legree, who has recorded 46 receptions for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. The Trojans' defensive line, led by true freshman Luke Wafle, Jide Abasiri, and Jahkeem Stewart, has been the strongest unit on USC’s defense this season and looks to have success against the Buckeyes' running back trio of Bo Jackson, Ja’Kobi Jackson, and Isaiah West.
